The bulk modulus is one of the most important properties of a solid. It is defined as the negative of the first derivative of the pressure-volume curve with respect to the volume. It is a measure of how stiff a solid is. A perfect crystal would have a bulk modulus of 1 i.e. it would be incompressible, while a perfect liquid would have a bulk modulus of 0 i.e. it would be incapable of sustaining any stress. In fact, the bulk modulus of a perfect solid is defined to be 1/2 the shear modulus.
